title: Comparing formulations by their LP bound

questions.stem: Two formulations of a crew-rostering rule allow the same 0/1 plans and use the same variables. Every row of formulation B is the sum of two rows of formulation A. The model maximizes. What follows for every objective?

options.text: A's search tree is never larger than B's, whatever the solver does
options.says: The page measured the opposite on GridCap small: the stronger front form took 82 nodes against 72, because the solver's presolve and cuts changed both models before branching.

options.text: A's LP bound is never higher than B's, whatever the objective
options.says: Right: a point that satisfies A's rows satisfies their sums, B's rows, so A's region lies inside B's, and a maximum over a smaller region is never higher.

options.text: A's best plan is worth less than B's, since A's rows are tighter
options.says: Both formulations allow the same 0/1 plans, so their MILP optima are equal; only the LP relaxations differ.

options.text: B's LP bound is never higher than A's, whatever the objective
options.says: That is the wrong way round: summing A's rows gives B's, so B's region contains A's and B's ceiling can only be higher.

origin.section: Containment Is Proved Row by Row: Each Weak Row Is a Sum of Strong Ones

questions.stem: A maximizing model has an LP bound of 1,200 in its old formulation and 1,080 in its new one; the best plan is worth 1,000. What share of the gap does the new formulation close?

options.text: 10%, the drop of 120 divided by the old bound of 1,200
options.says: The share is measured against the old gap, 1,200 - 1,000 = 200, not against the bound itself.

options.text: 12%, the drop of 120 divided by the best plan of 1,000
options.says: Dividing by the best plan gives a share of the plan's value; the gap closed divides by the old gap of 200.

options.text: 40%, the gap of 80 left over divided by the old gap of 200
options.says: 80 / 200 is the share still open; the share closed is the drop, 120, over the old gap, 200.

options.text: 60%, the drop of 120 divided by the old gap of 200

origin.section: The Share of the Gap Closed Puts Two Bounds on One Scale

questions.stem: A team replaces aggregated linking rows by disaggregated ones. The LP bound falls by 8%, yet HiGHS's bound after its root node is the same for both models and the stronger one takes more nodes. How does the page read this?

options.text: Presolve and the solver's cuts made up, before branching, what the weak rows lost
options.says: Right: the root bound is the bound after presolve and cuts, so equal root bounds mean the solver's own work closed the difference before branching, as on GridCap small.

options.text: The new rows must cut off some allowed plans, since a stronger form searches less
options.says: Both forms allow the same 0/1 plans (the page checks it on whole numbers), and a stronger formulation is no promise of a smaller search.

options.text: The LP bound must have been measured wrongly, since it equals the root bound
options.says: The LP bound is the formulation alone; the root bound comes after presolve and cuts, and the page shows them differ by thousands.

options.text: The weak form allows extra whole plans, so its search finds better ones sooner
options.says: With 0/1 values the aggregated row and the disaggregated rows allow exactly the same plans.

origin.section: The Solver's Root Bound Is the Second Measurement
